Hi John

Lets see if we can help you troubleshoot the issue.

Q1) Not Receiving Emails

The update is unlikely to have stopped you receiving email. It mostly contains bug fixes.

A. Can you confirm which version of Thunderbird for Android you're using.

     You can find this by navigating to: settings > about

B. Can you perform the below task. It tests the settings and server connection responsible for receiving mails.

     1. Navigate to settings > Account name "BT" > fetching mail > incoming server.      2. Tap next.

     Are any error messages displayed in the app or Android notification shade after the test?      Are there any prompts to sign-in?

C. Do you receive any emails when you manually sync the account, or see any error message?

     1. Tap the top left menu button to show your account folders      2. Tap the "sync account" button at the bottom of the list

Once you provide feedback on the above, I'll be better placed to direct you on further trouble shooting steps. Please respond on this ticket.

Q2) Spam Folder

Do you know what type of connection your account is using IMAP or POP?

     The app does support and display a spam folder. See the attached screen shot.      It's only available on IMAP connections. Pop doesn't support server folders / labels.

On the assumption you're using Imap but don't see either the spam folder or content within, check the following.

A.      1. Navigate to settings > account name > folders.      2. Check "Spam folder" is set = Automatic (Spam).      3. If the folder is assigned "None", tap and select your spam folder.

B.      1. Tap the top left menu button to show your account folders.      2. Tap manage folders (Bottom of the list).      3. Tap the spam folder.      4. Toggle "Enable Sync" ON.

Does the issue only occur in Firefox. Can you test using another browsers or app supporting mailto links?

What happens when you click a mailto link?

  • Nothing happens
  • You're redirected to a web page in the browser.
  • The link opens in another app such as gmail.
  • You see a message saying no app can perform this action.

Firefox

Firefox has some quirks around mailto links. When clicked, Firefox requests confirmation before passing to androids link handling. If you cancel the prompt, clicking the link again does nothing until you close the web page or browser. See screen shots.

Android

When clicking a mailto link, Android normally opens a box allowing you to select which app to open the link with. If you've previously set a default app via this box (ticked don't ask again), it will open automatically.

To reset this default app so you can pick Thunderbird ...

  1. Open Android settings > Apps.
  2. Tap the name of the app currently opening mailto links.
  3. Look for "open by default" or a similar setting (varies by phone / Android version).
  4. Tap clear default preferences.

There's no in app setting within Thunderbird Android to enable / disable its link handling.
